event.asset: DEA COVID-era telemedicine flexibilities for prescribing controlled substances
event.title: COVID-era telemedicine flexibilities for controlled-substance prescribing lapse and the in-person requirement returns
event.proposition: The COVID-era telemedicine flexibilities for prescribing controlled substances expire at the end of the COVID-19 public health emergency without a DEA extension, so the Ryan Haight Act in-person visit requirement applies again to telehealth patients.
event.criterion: TRUE on the expiry date of the COVID-19 public health emergency if no DEA rule or order extending the COVID-era telemedicine flexibilities for prescribing controlled substances has been published in the Federal Register (or announced by DEA) by that date, so that the Ryan Haight Act in-person visit requirement applies again to telehealth patients from the next day. FALSE if such an extension is published by that date.
readings: 'The Ryan Haight Act returns', 'in-office visits return for everybody everywhere' and an 'instant' return to in-person providers are read as the in-person requirement applying again to all telehealth controlled-substance patients at the PHE end.

event.asset: DEA COVID-era telemedicine flexibilities for prescribing controlled substances
event.title: DEA extends the COVID-era telemedicine flexibilities for controlled-substance prescribing
event.proposition: DEA issues a rule or order that extends the COVID-era telemedicine flexibilities for prescribing controlled substances beyond the end of the COVID-19 public health emergency.
event.criterion: TRUE on the Federal Register publication date (or the DEA announcement date, if earlier) of a temporary rule or order that extends the COVID-era telemedicine flexibilities for prescribing controlled substances beyond the end of the COVID-19 public health emergency. A proposed rule is not an extension. A lapse of the flexibilities, with the Ryan Haight Act in-person requirement applying again, resolves FALSE.
readings: Any DEA rule or order that continues remote prescribing of controlled substances without an in-person visit past the PHE end counts as an extension.
